note.question: How much connectivity should a matching platform permit when longer consideration sets intensify competition but can improve match rates at the cost of search effort and unequal partner quality?
note.overview: The paper formally characterizes stable matching outcomes in partially connected two-sided markets and uses those equilibrium characterizations to design consideration-set and preference-list connectivity.

objects: Agents on the two sides of a matching market

The analytical environment uses a random bipartite graph and independent uniform ordinal preferences
The platform designs connectivity using distributional market primitives rather than each realized preference

Proposing-side agents make deferred-acceptance proposals according to their rankings

components.label: Men-optimal stable matching under deferred acceptance
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Men-optimal stable matching under deferred acceptance. A matching is stable when no mutually preferable blocking pair exists. The analysis characterizes the men-optimal stable matching produced by men-proposing deferred acceptance and uses simulations to assess proximity to the women-optimal stable matching.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: The platform chooses a connectivity intervention; a random consideration graph and strict preferences are realized; one side proposes under deferred acceptance; the induced men-optimal stable matching is evaluated by ranks, unmatched counts, and welfare. Connectivity controls which partners can be considered before deferred acceptance runs. Below the transition, both sides have similar partner ranks and many agents may remain unmatched; above it, the short side gains a marked rank advantage.
